name: Convert the fallen
summary: Your attacks or an aura tag enemy soldiers while they keep being hit or stay in range. A tagged soldier cannot receive buffs from its own side, and if it dies while tagged it rises as a weak minion for you, in some games a resource as well. Vehicles and machines cannot be tagged, and what rises is a new, lesser unit rather than the victim: only the dead change sides. Teammates' kills count too, so the tag rewards focus fire around its source. Some versions put a short curse on one target, so the kill must come quickly; others raise copies of the latest kills on a key. Unlike mind-control it never takes a living unit; unlike leech-weapon-on-kill it gains bodies, not weapons; unlike execute-target's spawn-from-victim twist, the kill itself is ordinary and the tag decides what rises.
counterplay: Fight it with vehicles and machines: in Tempest Rising only infantry can be Subjugated, so armour feeds it nothing.
Pull tagged soldiers back rather than letting them die there: a soldier who leaves the aura, or outlives a short curse, rises as nothing.
Clear the minions with splash: they are weak and come in clumps, and Halo Wars 2 players beat the Flood's swarms with area damage.
Deny the body: in Warcraft III magic-immune units are untouched by the curse, and a unit its own side sacrifices first spawns nothing; in Halo, breaking up a body stops it being raised.
Kill or outrange the source: the aura carrier or the tagging units are the root, so burst them first or fight from beyond their reach.
Keep buffs for untagged soldiers: a boost on a tagged soldier is wasted.

other_examples.unit: Subjugation (Subjugator, Warden, Combat Servitor, War Ender, Sanctifier, Seeker)
other_examples.note: The Veti status the Vimana and the Enlightened share with other units: the Subjugator's spike missiles tag the infantry they hit (when it fights against the player in the other two campaigns it carries a Subjugation aura instead), and the Warden, the Combat Servitor, the War Ender's Spike Barrage, the Sanctifier's aura and, with a doctrine, the Seeker apply it too. Tagged infantry cannot receive positive effects and become Enlightened if they are killed. Doctrines widen the auras and, at the fifth step, make the tag also silence its victims and slow their attacks.

sources.title: Doctrine, Tempest Rising Wiki
sources.note: Aura Amplifiers and Vile Subjugation in the Veti Subjugation tree.

other_examples.note: An attack bonus the hero can switch on: each arrow adds damage, and an enemy that dies within a couple of seconds of being hit rises as a Dark Minion for her, a lesser one at first and stronger with each level, weaker than a normal raised skeleton. Only units that leave a corpse count, magic-immune units are unaffected, and an undead unit its owner sacrifices first spawns nothing. Players build a skeleton army with it while clearing neutral camps, and her Life Drain applies the same effect since a later patch.

other_examples.note: In Halo Wars 2's Flood content a unit is infected only when it is killed, and from a Grunt squad only the leader comes back; infected vehicles lose their abilities and every infected unit drops back to the lowest upgrade level. Swarms of infection forms die easily to splash damage.

shooter_analogues.note: On a key, Nekros raises shadow copies of the enemies that he and his shadows killed most recently, strongest first; kills by teammates do not count. The copies keep their stats with a bonus, lose a share of their health every second, draw enemy fire, are healed by casting again, and wither inside the enemy's nullifier bubbles.

sources.title: Shadows of the Dead, Warframe Wiki

shooter_analogues.note: Survivors who die switch to the zombie team, which usually fights with melee that kills in one hit; when one survivor is left, that player can be given special traits, such as being marked for the zombies.
A randomly chosen player starts on the infected side, and each survivor who is killed switches to it; the round ends when the clock expires or no survivor is left.

player_translation.summary: A curse or aura that turns the enemy's losses into your reinforcements. Tagged enemy soldiers glow and cannot be buffed, and any that die while tagged leave behind a weak AI minion that fights for your team for a short while. Players never change sides; only an AI husk rises from the body.
as_user: Your weapon's hits, or an aura around you, tag enemy soldiers for a few seconds; the tag refreshes while you keep hitting them or while they stay in range.
Tagged soldiers shrug off their team's buffs (speed, armour or damage boosts), so you are at your best against a buffed push.

When a tagged enemy dies, by your hand or a teammate's, a minion rises at the body after a short delay: a weak AI soldier on your side that attacks enemies nearby and crumbles after a while. Only a few can be alive at once; the oldest crumbles when a new one rises.
Vehicles and machines cannot be tagged. The minions are fodder, not an army: a moment of pressure or a screen for your team.
as_target: A tagged soldier gets a clear mark (golden rays, as Tempest Rising shows it) and a HUD icon, and buffs from teammates visibly fizzle on it.
Step out of the aura or away from the tagger and the tag fades after a few seconds; if you die untagged, nothing rises.
If you die tagged you respawn as usual; the minion is an AI copy, so your team should clear it fast, ideally with splash.
teammates: The tagger's team focuses fire on tagged soldiers, since every kill is worth a minion: a setup-and-finish between the tagger and the damage dealers.
The victim's team keeps its buffs for untagged teammates, brings vehicles against the tagger and clears minions with splash.
Minions count for the whole team, so a teammate's kill on a tagged enemy pays off for everyone.
controls: No key for the base pattern: the tag rides on the primary weapon or comes from an always-on aura.
Death-curse variant: Q fires a curse at one enemy; if it dies before the curse ends, its minion rises. One counted key.
Raise-the-latest variant: Q raises copies of the last few enemies you killed, on a long cooldown.
feedback: Tagged enemies carry a coloured glow and an icon that both teams see, and a refused buff makes a small fizzle.
The aura's reach is a soft ring around its carrier for its own team and a tinted edge for enemies inside it.
A rising minion plays a short animation and sound at the body, and minions wear the team colour with a dimmer, distinct silhouette so nobody takes them for players.
A small HUD counter shows how many minions are alive and the cap.
changes_from_rts: In Tempest Rising the risen soldiers become full Enlightened units and a resource; in a shooter the dead enemy is a person who respawns, so only a weak, short-lived AI minion rises at the body.
The infantry-only rule stays: a destroyed vehicle rising for the other team would need a pilot and would swing too much.
The buff block stays, but from above it needs an icon so players can see why a teammate's boost did nothing.
RTS armies are capped only by supply; here a small cap and a lifetime per minion keep the map readable and the server light.
As in Tempest Rising, any death while tagged counts, whoever lands the kill, which turns a passive aura into team play.

team_play.notes: The tag pays off only when the team turns tagged soldiers into kills, and every such kill adds a minion for the whole team. The victims' team answers with vehicles, splash and spacing, and keeps its buffers' work for untagged teammates.

notes: A status tag with a timer, refreshed by hits or by standing in an aura, and a rule that refuses incoming buffs while it lasts.
On death, spawn an AI minion at the body with a simple behaviour (follow its owner, attack the nearest enemy), a lifetime and a cap per owner.
AI minions need pathfinding, targeting and network sync, so they must stay cheap and few.
Ownership and credit rules: whose minion it is, and who scores its kills.
It snowballs: the side that is winning fights raises more minions, so keep them weak, short-lived and capped.
A wide aura that blocks every buff can make enemy buffers useless near its carrier; the radius is the lever.
Stacking several taggers multiplies minions; the cap should be per team as well as per player.
Minions must never be mistaken for players, or for the victim coming back.
Players need to see which of them are tagged and why a buff failed.
In a big fight many tags and minions at once can swamp the screen.

variants.name: Tag on hit
variants.summary: Each hit of your weapon tags the enemy soldier for a few seconds. The default.
variants.seen_in: Tempest Rising Enlightened and Subjugator (Subjugating Attack)

variants.name: Tagging aura
variants.summary: An always-on aura tags every enemy soldier in a wide circle around you.
variants.seen_in: Tempest Rising Vimana and Sanctifier (Subjugation Aura)

variants.name: Death curse
variants.summary: A short curse on the enemy you hit, adding a little damage: if it dies before the curse ends, a minion rises, stronger as the curse is upgraded.
variants.seen_in: Warcraft III Dark Ranger's Black Arrow

variants.name: Silencing tag
variants.summary: The tag also blocks the victim's abilities and slows its attacks while it lasts.

variants.name: Raise the latest
variants.summary: On a key, raise copies of the last few enemies you killed; they keep their stats with a bonus, draw enemy fire and wither over time, and casting again heals them.
variants.seen_in: Warframe Nekros's Shadows of the Dead

variants.name: Spreading tag
variants.summary: The risen minions carry the tag themselves, so every enemy soldier they hit can rise in turn.
variants.seen_in: Tempest Rising (risen Enlightened keep the Subjugating Attack); Halo and Call of Duty infection modes

adds_strengths.why: Enemy soldiers that die tagged come back as minions on its side, and buffs on tagged soldiers are wasted.

adds_weaknesses.why: Does nothing to vehicles and machines, and its minions are weak and short-lived.

counters.why: Only soldiers can be tagged, and each one that dies tagged turns into a minion against its own team.
A buffer's boosts do nothing for tagged soldiers.

countered_by.why: Vehicles cannot be tagged, so they fight it without feeding it minions and run the weak minions down.
Splash clears the weak, clumped minions quickly, as Halo Wars 2 players do against the Flood.
Long-range fire hits the tagger from beyond its aura or reach, so no tagged soldier dies near it.

open_questions: Should a risen minion be a generic weak soldier (the proposal here) or a copy of the victim's unit, as Warframe's shadows are?
Who owns the minion when a teammate lands the killing blow on a tagged enemy: the tagger, the killer or the team?
Does the buff block include heals, or only status boosts such as speed and armour? Tempest Rising blocks positive status effects.
Should vehicle crews be taggable, so that a destroyed vehicle's crew rises, or stay immune as Tempest Rising's infantry-only rule has it?
Is a team resource gain wanted on top of the minion, as Tempest Rising's Enlightened are both a unit and a resource?

Should execute-target's spawn-from-victim variant, where the killing strike itself hatches minions for the attacker, move here as a variant or stay there? The two share their result, so the merge pass can decide.

shooter_fit.reason: Warframe shows raised minions working in a co-op shooter and infection modes are popular, but against players the dead stay themselves, so only a weak AI minion rises. The buff block reads well with an icon; minion clutter from a top-down view is the main risk.
